resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.lead_time: Standard inspections are scheduled by the office; an expedited inspection (3 days or less) costs a $100 surcharge, pending availability.
resale_co.valid_for: 90 days from the initial inspection for sales (30 days for rentals)
requirements: No open permits (checked on the application)

Exterior: property clean and free of rubbish; grass and bushes trimmed; sidewalks, driveway and driveway apron free of cracks, raised sections and trip hazards; garages, sheds, fences, retaining walls and pools sound

Exterior structure weathertight with no peeling paint or rotting boards; chimney caps on fireplace chimneys; handrails on 4 or more risers and guardrails over 30 inches; house numbers at least 4 inches tall
Windows open, stay open and have screens; exit doors and windows open without a key or tool
Interior surfaces clean and sound; bathrooms without windows need mechanical ventilation; tubs and showers need shower rods
Plumbing working with hot water able to reach 110 degrees F
Electrical: required outlets and light fixtures; GFI outlets in bathrooms, laundry rooms and within 6 feet of a sink
Dryer transition duct must be a single listed UL 2158A duct, 8 feet or less, not concealed
Heating and Hot Water Heater Certification signed by a licensed plumber or certified heating contractor; heat able to keep 68 degrees F
For homes built before 1978: a lead Certification of Clearance from the Freehold Area Health Department before the CCO is issued (see other items)

fees.label: CCO inspection, 1 and 2 family dwellings (including condo and townhouse)
Expedited CCO inspection (3 days or less), surcharge
fees.quote: Expedited Inspection (3 days or less) $100 SURCHARGE Pending Availability

fees.label: Second and later CCO re-inspections (first re-inspection free)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Residential Certificate of Continued Occupancy and Smoke Detector Certificate (one combined Borough packet), give the tentative closing date, and pay by cash, check or money order payable to "Borough of Freehold" at the Code Enforcement Office, 30 Mechanic Street, Freehold. Include the heating and hot water heater certification from a licensed contractor. An adult must be present for the inspection.

evidence.quote: APPLICATION FOR RESIDENTIAL CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUED OCCUPANCY & SMOKE DETECTOR CERTIFICATE
-C/O Expiration Dates: 90 days from initial inspection for sales; 30 days for rentals

This new ordinance requires a Certification of Clearance issued by the Freehold Area Health Department prior to issuances of a Continued Certificate of Occupancy for resale, rental or change of occupancy on all residential properties.

resale_co.notes: The Borough code is on municode, which could not be read here, so the requirement rests on the Borough's own CCO application (which lists "Sale" as a reason for the change of occupancy and a 90-day sale expiration) and the 2022 Borough notice about the Freehold Area Health Department lead clearance before a resale CCO. The application PDF is a scan; quotes are taken from its text layer. The Code Enforcement page hides staff emails behind a protection script, so no email is listed; the decoded mailto for the Director slot pointed to a different name, so it was left out. Other Code Enforcement staff: Michael Mulcahy and Anas Sohail (Code Enforcement Officers), Rebecca Ponder (Code Enforcement Clerk). The landlord registration program and the LEW Environmental lead-safe program for rentals are rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms per the date the home was built or renovated (10-year sealed battery alarms on all levels for homes before January 1977, up to hardwired, interconnected alarms with battery backup on all levels and in each bedroom for homes from March 1991); AC-powered alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarms outside every separate sleeping area

Secondary power source label ("CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER", not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and electric meter if the home has a generator, solar panels, battery storage or another supplemental source
An adult 18 or older must be present for the inspection

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Alarm, and Secondary Power Source Compliance (part of the Borough's CCO packet) with the closing date and email addresses for the certificate, and submit it to the Freehold Borough Fire Bureau, 30 Mechanic St, Freehold. After a failed inspection the applicant must call to request a new appointment.

fire_cert.notes: Fees come from the Fire Bureau application inside the Borough's scanned CCO packet; the scan's text layer runs "CSDCMAC" and "received" together, and quotes copy it as is. The 3-business-day tier is the Borough's own schedule, not the state's 10-day tiers. The packet's checklist lists smoke and CO rules under "Rental use only" and mentions an NFPA-recommended fire extinguisher, but the Fire Bureau application itself covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and secondary power labels only, consistent with P.L.2025, c.19.

other_items.label: Lead Certification of Clearance (homes built before 1978)
other_items.detail: Under Freehold Borough Ordinance 8.56.285, owners of homes built before 1978 that are changing ownership or occupancy must get a certification of clearance from the Freehold Area Health Department (1 Municipal Plaza, 732-294-2060) before the CCO is issued. The Health Department's certified inspectors inspect free of charge on Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9 am to 12 pm, or a NJ licensed private lead inspector may be used; lead-free documentation is also accepted.

other_items.label: Heating and hot water heater certification
other_items.detail: A licensed plumber or certified heating contractor must fill out the Borough's Heating System and Hot Water Heater Certification for the CCO; fireplaces need a chimney certification.

other_items.label: Sidewalks and driveway aprons
other_items.detail: The CCO checklist requires sidewalks, driveways and driveway aprons to be free of cracks, raised sections or trip hazards; the Borough posts a separate sidewalk and apron replacement permit.
